service.clear.explain: Clears this service's cache and site data: HTTP cache, localStorage, IndexedDB, Cache Storage and service workers. Cookies and other services are left alone. A service that keeps its sign-in in localStorage will sign you out of it. Its service worker is removed, so web push notifications that depend on it need subscribing again. Scripts and styles this tab has already loaded may still be used; if the service still looks out of date afterwards, reload the console page.

help.title: Connection help · for you and your agent
help.intro: Use the form for a web page, a built-in plugin for a supported service, or a plugin folder for a custom integration.
help.pages.title: Connect a web page
help.pages.step1: Start the service and check that its address opens in your browser. For example, http://127.0.0.1:3000/. hostdeck does not start the service for you.
help.pages.step2: In the form below, choose Embed for a web page on this machine or the local network. Choose Link to open any HTTP or HTTPS address in a new tab.
help.pages.step3: Enter its address and an optional name, then choose Add. It appears immediately; open it from the sidebar. Dragging an address onto the console also adds an embedded page.
help.plugins.title: Connect a plugin
help.plugins.step1: For a built-in plugin below, read its setup instructions, start its service if needed, then choose Add and confirm. It takes effect immediately.
help.plugins.step2: For a custom plugin, create a uniquely named folder (for example, my-service) inside the actual plugin directory below, and save plugin.yaml in it. This example reads the status field of a JSON response; replace the address and field with your service’s values.
help.plugins.step3: Restart hostdeck using the same data directory and address after adding or editing files by command. Refreshing the browser alone does not reload them. Check Pages & plugins for loading errors, then check the card or page.
help.plugins.trust: Only use plugin programs you trust: they run with your permissions. Custom plugins can provide JSON cards and details or connect existing web pages; they do not serve their own HTML. schema: 1 is implemented, but the format may change before the first release.
help.agent.title: Let an agent connect it
help.agent.intro: Copy a prompt into an agent that can run commands on this computer. Then tell it the service name, address and what you want to show. Copying only copies text; it does not change your data.
help.agent.copied: Prompt copied. Paste it into your agent and describe the service to connect.
help.agent.copyFailed: Could not access the clipboard. The prompt is selected below; copy it manually.
help.agent.pages: Connect an existing web page. First check that its address opens. proxy embeds HTTP/HTTPS pages on this machine or the local network; link opens any HTTP/HTTPS page in a new tab. hostdeck does not start the external service. Use POST /api/pages with JSON fields address, name and mode; the Origin header must equal the console origin. The example adds an embedded page immediately and writes its plugin.yaml in the actual plugin directory. Before adding, GET /api/catalog and check installed entries to avoid duplicates. To edit an existing page, use POST /api/plugins/<id>/page with only the requested fields: name, icon, proxy OR link, and cardUrl only for an existing HTTP card. Back up its plugin.yaml first, retain comments, commands and other settings. Send requests only to the selected local console; do not weaken Origin checks.
help.agent.plugins: Connect a custom plugin. Prefer an appropriate built-in plugin when available: GET /api/catalog lists available IDs and setup instructions; POST /api/catalog/<id> with the console Origin adds it immediately. Otherwise create plugins/<unique-id>/plugin.yaml inside this instance’s data directory. The plugin directory listed above already ends in plugins; do not append plugins a second time. Check both <id> and .<id> to avoid replacing an enabled or disabled plugin. For existing plugins, back up the entire folder before modifying only the requested manifest fields or scripts, preserving comments, commands and unrelated values. The following commands create a new my-service/plugin.yaml, refusing existing folders. The sample expects a JSON endpoint returning a status field: replace its URL, field and name. Never overwrite an existing plugin with this sample.
help.agent.contract: Current manifest contract (schema: 1; may change before the first release): name is required; provide at least one of page, card or detail. page has proxy OR link; page and detail cannot coexist, but either can have a card. card.http makes a GET request; value and optional rows use gjson paths; label is display text; interval defaults to 1m; warn/error each select one of above, below, equals or not. card.exec.command is an argv array; exec.windows replaces it on Windows. Commands run in the plugin folder and print only JSON to stdout, diagnostics to stderr. Card JSON: {"status":"ok","value":42,"label":"Count","rows":[{"name":"Queue","value":3,"status":"warn"}]} or {"error":"Reason"}. detail.exec prints {"items":[{"id":"item-1","name":"Item","status":"ok","value":"ready","fields":[{"name":"Path","value":"/example"}],"log":"text","actions":[{"id":"open","label":"Open"}]}]}. actions requires detail; actions.exec receives <action-id> <item-id> and may print {"message":"Done"} or {"error":"Reason"}. Human text can be a string or an object keyed by en and zh-CN. Windows PowerShell scripts use UTF-8 with BOM and output UTF-8. Only run trusted programs; plugins have the user’s permissions. Secrets in HTTP URLs/headers must be ${env:NAME}, supplied to the hostdeck process; never put tokens in files or output. Do not change layout.json, ports.json or other plugins as part of this connection.
help.agent.finish: After manual file changes, restart hostdeck with its original data directory and listening address through its existing launch method. There is no reload CLI command or reload-only HTTP endpoint. A browser refresh does not reload plugin files; do not toggle an unrelated plugin just to trigger reload. If a restart would interrupt work and is not authorized, report that files are saved and restart is pending. API additions and edits reload immediately; do not restart for them. Validate via GET /api/catalog (installed[].loaded, broken and error), GET /api/plugins, GET /api/cards and GET /api/detail/<id> as applicable, then open the page or card. Report files changed, commands run and actual verification; distinguish saved data from a working integration. Do not claim success if the service is unreachable.
